issue.title: Empty series should be automatically deleted in Dashboard

license.name: GNU Affero General Public License v3.0

issue.body:
**To Reproduce**

Create a unique series name for any post.
That adds a particular series name in Dashboard. So far so good.

Edit the same post and remove the series.
Go back and check the Dashboard. The series name is still there and says ["your_series_name"] (0 Part Series).

![chrome_xqNhRp9DTd](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/42511917/92034771-61be3280-ed76-11ea-8037-b41fe10c0b84.png)


**Expected behavior**

If the series is empty, it should be automatically removed from Dashboard.
As the user can make it anytime later if he decides. No need to keep around empty ones.

issue.title: User can't remove empty series from dashboard view

license.name: GNU Affero General Public License v3.0

issue.body:
**Describe the bug**

When a user views series from their dashboard (i.e. https://dev.to/yourusername/series) they're able to see "0 Part Series" for posts that they've drafted in a series but perhaps deleted for some reason along the way.

There's no way to delete the 0 part series and it doesn't seem like these should exist here in the first place.

**To Reproduce**

1. Create 2 posts under the same series
2. Unpublish and delete both posts
3. Navigate to your user dashboard (https://dev.to/dashboard)
4. Scroll down to "series" in the lefthand column and click on it (i.e. https://dev.to/yourusername/series)
5. You should see the series name you just created with "(0 part series)" beside it

**Expected behavior**

Only published multi-part series should appear in this list. It's debatable that drafted series should appear in the list too. But if a series has been deleted, then it should not appear in the list.

If 0 part series must appear in the list, then they should be deletable by the user.

**Screenshots**

![Image 2020-09-16 at 5 42 54 PM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/16007075/93395455-f54a3580-f843-11ea-980d-e129540f703d.png)

**Additional context**

This came about because a user wrote in asking how to remove an empty series.
